   475	
   476	## E5 — Persistent RenderScene and v0.1-alpha
   477	
   478	**Goal:** stop rebuilding and uploading all object data merely because the next frame has begun.
   479	
   480	The Skyrim blog proposes a persistent GPU scene representation with event-driven updates instead of repeatedly traversing the game graph [S7]. Here, that idea is introduced incrementally: persistent state and correct changes first; GPU visibility arrives only in E7.
   481	
   482	### E5.1. Persistent state on the Bend side
   483	
   484	- [ ] Create an independent RenderScene with tables of instances, transforms/bounds, mesh/material references, and loading state.
   485	- [ ] Define a `Create / Update / Remove` protocol. Handle render-component addition and removal, despawn, mesh/material changes, and parent changes.
   486	- [ ] Use Bendvy's public change/removal mechanisms or an explicit observation adapter. Do not assume a `Changed` query necessarily runs in O(number of changes).
   487	- [ ] Give each render slot a stable identity. A stale update must not alter a new object after slot reuse; generation/ID overflow has an explicit failure policy or a safe ID-space renewal policy.
   488	- [ ] Preserve a full rebuild as a debugging reference and recovery path, not as normal per-frame work.
   489	- [ ] Compare incremental state with a full ECS projection for identical committed states. Comparison uses logical IDs rather than requiring identical element placement in memory.
   490	
   491	### E5.2. Persistent GPU resources and revisions
   492	
   493	- [ ] Retain mesh/material/object data between frames. Existing buffers/descriptors and CPU-issued draws are acceptable initially.
   494	- [ ] Before storing the complete table in one GPU-readable buffer, check API capabilities; if needed, add storage buffers as a separate minimal extension rather than claiming they already exist.
   495	- [ ] Separate object data from camera/view data: moving the camera does not trigger re-uploading unchanged meshes or object transforms.
   496	- [ ] Upload dirty ranges after the E3 check; record upload volume and count.
   497	- [ ] Start with correct single-threaded application of changes at the frame boundary. A separate render thread and a lock-free mailbox are not required.
   498	- [ ] With multiple frame slots, track the applied revision of each dataset and do not modify memory still in use by the GPU.
   499	- [ ] Clear the change log only after the necessary consumer acknowledgments, or replace it with a complete consistent revision. Skipping a frame must not lose an object removal.
   500	- [ ] If delta packets are introduced later, include `base_revision` and `new_revision`. A base mismatch triggers replay/resync rather than silently applying the latest delta.
   501	- [ ] Distinguish prepared data, successfully queued uploads, and completed use. A backend error must not falsely acknowledge an applied revision.
   502	
   503	**Important:** a mailbox of complete revisions and a delta queue are different protocols. “Take only the latest message” is not valid for every sequence of changes. This is not a reason to immediately introduce shared memory/zero-copy.
   504	
   505	### E5.3. Measurements and acceptance
   506	
   507	- [ ] Check a static scene; camera-only movement; changes to a small subset of objects; movement of every object; frequent spawn/despawn and resource replacement.
   508	- [ ] After the initial population of all active frame slots, a static scene does not repack or re-upload unchanged object data. Camera uniforms and other actual changes are accounted for separately.
   509	- [ ] Measure separately: N inspected ECS elements, K changed objects, bytes uploaded, CPU visibility, and draw preparation. A small K does not prove that all CPU work has become O(K).
   510	- [ ] Preserve a correct CPU-culling/direct-draw path. Traversal for visibility remains acceptable; this stage aims to eliminate unnecessary state reconstruction and uploads, not to claim zero CPU cost.
   511	- [ ] Automate proofs, headless tests, builds, and available GPU/window checks; an absent GPU means “not performed,” not success.
   512	- [ ] Document installation, the API, limitations, dependencies, and licenses for code/demo assets in use.
   513	- [ ] Check both non-voxel applications from a clean environment and release `v0.1-alpha`.
   514	
   515	**Done when:** both programs run without core changes; RenderScene matches the reference projection; unchanged data is not re-uploaded; updates and removals are not lost; checks are reproducible.
   516	
   517	**Out of scope:** mandatory `bend-voxel` migration, a render graph, compute culling, multi-draw, a multithreaded mailbox, or beating Bevy in FPS.
   518

   521	## E6 — Verifiable render graph
   522	
   523	**Prerequisite:** a working alpha and several real passes with dependencies. For example: shadow pass → main pass → postprocess. Do not add an effect solely to manufacture a graph.
   524	
   525	**Goal:** Bend builds an executable plan from pass and resource descriptions. Separating the graph from the GPU API follows an idea similar to OpenRenderGraph/BasicRHI, but this implementation is a small Bend module [S8].

Trail 28 is open and has no attached `changes[]` in live show output. This is a delivery-record discrepancy, not missing implementation.
- **Trail lifecycle is distinct from merge:** workflow Trail 27 and OBJ Trail 26 remain open; both bodies say unmerged, while their live changes report `merged`: [workflow change 24](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/27/changes/entangle/24), [OBJ change 23](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/26/changes/entangle/23). Baseline [change 5](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/6/changes/entangle/5) is also merged under open Trail 6. An autonomous loop must inspect source and live change state instead of rewarding closed Trails or optimistic text.

Concrete lessons from November 3–4 evidence:

- **Wrong-layer qualification loses semantics.** Jonlib’s `assemble.meshes` facade lost default/named materials; Entangle instead consumes validated commands and attributes. Independent retained asset specifications supply the oracle, avoiding parser-vs-parser agreement. [OBJ evidence](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/verification/2026-11-04-model-obj/README.md:62)
- **A nonzero exit can be irrelevant.** Mutation acceptance requires the named property failure, followed by restored-source success. Timeouts, compile failures and import rejection do not count. The upload proof’s first symlink-based mutation attempt failed import validation before checking the theorem; the real-copy attempt caught the intended guard removal. [Upload evidence](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/verification/2026-11-03-upload-range/README.md:19), [workflow contract](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/development.md:11)
- **Shared working directories contaminated verification scope.** Workflow validation copied a concurrent OBJ invocation without its implementation; source snapshots also initially retained invalid submodule Git paths. Both were corrected, failed attempts retained. Existing PNG and later JSON imports separately exposed missing dependency-policy registration. [Workflow corrections](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/verification/2026-11-04-development-workflow/README.md:11)
- **Historical green does not certify HEAD.** The thirteen-stage workflow run preceded OBJ; publication reran seven proof-profile stages. JSON’s ten-stage `json` receipt passed on its snapshot, but a later full-native invocation was interrupted at exit 143 and explicitly is not a pass. [Workflow scope](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/verification/2026-11-04-development-workflow/README.md:45), [JSON limits](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/verification/2026-11-04-json-scene/README.md:21)
- **No demonstrated optimization yet.** The existing baseline predates fixed timestep, used one Bend worker with GPU dispatch disabled, and measured real Vulkan graphics. Instrumentation overhead and simulation/extraction limiters remain unresolved; no thread-count or GPU-lane scaling study exists. Its attempt-cap defect was corrected using real 151-success/150-rejection runs. [Baseline boundaries](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/baseline-measurements.md:71), [measurement limitations](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/docs/baseline-measurements.md:126)

**Recommended first campaign:** a bounded E4 textured-model vertical slice: one retained model plus decoded PNG, UV attributes, engine-owned upload/sampler/material lifetime, and visible output through the existing camera/window path. First qualify the actual native texture API with independently known pixel/layout output. Keep one owner for coupled implementation/laws/verifier. Acceptance should include source-to-render correspondence, exact offscreen pixels, live window capture/replay, release/replacement and missing/corrupt asset recovery, zero-object cleanup, and named production mutation controls. This directly advances the [next incomplete E4 item](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/ROADMAP_updated_v6_EN.md:458); it should not claim all of E4 complete.

Later E5 offers a better hillclimbing objective than FPS: preserve equality with a full ECS projection while reducing unchanged object packing/upload, separately recording inspected `N`, changed `K`, accepted upload bytes/calls, and draw preparation. The roadmap already specifies [reference equivalence](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/ROADMAP_updated_v6_EN.md:484) and [observable metrics](/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/ROADMAP_updated_v6_EN.md:507).

Evidence gap: Trail show returns bodies and live changes but no separate historical findings collection. A read-only fallback findings endpoint returned 404; findings above come from retained repository verification records, not an asserted complete Entire findings audit.
